title: introduce-anchored-rope-prefetch-attn-bridge-hotpath-scheduler
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Introduce an anchored-rope prefetcher and attention-bridge hotpath scheduler that reduce tail latency and improve throughput for long-context workloads. Backward compatible, falls back to existing kernels when needed.
description:
Motivation and summary: Long-sequence streaming workloads still suffer from tail-latency spikes due to rotary/rope rematerialization and KV cache misses during continuous batching. This PR introduces two complementary runtime features: (1) an "anchored-rope prefetcher" that anchors rotary/rope offsets to streaming lanes and proactively warms per-lane KV segments, and (2) an "attention-bridge" microkernel path with a hotpath scheduler that routes short-latency streaming requests to a fused rotary+qkv transform with minimal memory movement. Together these reduce p50/p95/p99 latency and increase steady-state throughput for mixed streaming and batched workloads.

What changed (high level):
- runtime/attention/attn_bridge.cu: new attention-bridge microkernel that applies fused rotary transforms on pinned buffers and calls the existing flash-backed matmul path. The bridge minimizes device->device memcpy and reorders transforms to enable earlier KV population.
- runtime/kv/anchored_prefetcher.cpp / .h: implementation of anchored-lane prefetcher, lane bookkeeping, and adaptive reservoir eviction. Prefetcher exposes lane affinity hints to the scheduler.
- runtime/scheduler/hotpath_scheduler.cpp: continuous batching scheduler extension that creates "hotpath lanes" for low-latency streams and uses lane-aware batching windows. Includes admission control and graceful fallback to default batcher.
- runtime/config/feature_flags.yaml: flags to toggle anchored prefetcher and bridge kernel independently for dogfooding.
- python/tests/test_anchor_rope.py: unit/integration tests covering lane affinity, KV warming, and fallback.
- perf/benchmarks/anchored_rope_trace.json: synthetic trace used for perf numbers and CI benchmark.
- docs/perf/anchored-rope-prefetch.md: design rationale and guidance for tuning lane counts and eviction thresholds.

Performance results (summary):
- Workloads: Llama-style 32k-token synthetic traces and 1:many real streaming traces from internal RL agent traces (anonymized).
- Median latency (seq=1024): -12% vs baseline (continuous-batcher + existing kernels)
- Throughput improvement (mixed streaming + batch): +20% steady-state tokens/sec under typical load
- p99 tail latency (seq=4096, streaming prioritization): -30% (most visible in mixed low-qps streaming lanes)
- Cost estimate: ~15% lower per-token GPU compute due to improved KV reuse and reduced redundant rotary ops

Compatibility and safety:
- Feature flags allow gradual rollout per-customer and per-cluster.
- If the bridge kernel or prefetcher detect unrecognized model layouts (legacy QKV packing), they fall back to existing kernels.
- We added unit tests that assert numeric closeness (relative error thresholds) between bridge path and baseline flash path for representative layers.

Review conversation (high-level):
- Miguel Torres (reviewer): "Nice design; main concern is memory amplification from per-lane KV reservoirs under many concurrent streams. Can we cap resident lane pages and add backpressure?"
- Author (Asha): "Added reservoir cap with LRU-proportional eviction and admission control in hotpath scheduler. See anchored_prefetcher.cpp:EvictIfOverBudget(). Also added metric kv.lane_resident_pages to monitor."
- Liam Chen (reviewer): "Bench results look promising. Please add an end-to-end CI run against the collector traces and confirm no regression on small-batch throughput."
- Author: "Triggered an extended perf job: perf-ci/anchored-rope on 2026-02-25; results attached to the CI. Small-batch microbench unchanged or slightly improved due to earlier rotary fusion."
- Sarah Nguyen (approver): "Code looks clean; I approve once the perf CI is green and we add the doc section on tuning lane count."

Rollout plan:
1) Merge behind feature flags (this PR).
2) Canary on Dedicated clusters with small lane_count (2) and reservoir_budget=16GB for a week. Monitor metrics: kv.lane_hit_rate, kv.lane_resident_pages, scheduler.hotpath_miss_rate, inference.p99
3) Gradually increase lane_count for streaming-heavy customers and tune eviction thresholds using the provided scripts in docs/perf.

Known limitations and follow-ups:
- Current bridge kernel assumes rotary is applied per-head in a single contiguous buffer; follow-up will add non-contiguous head layout support (ENG-2201).
- Prefetcher warms at lane granularity; future work: sub-lane warm granularity for very large models to reduce resident memory footprint.

Merge: Squash-merged into main on 2026-02-28 after perf CI turned green and approvals from Miguel and Sarah.

Notes for on-call / SRE: If rollout causes increased OOMs, disable "anchored_prefetcher" flag and set scheduler.hotpath_enabled=false. Metrics exposed: kv.lane_resident_pages, kv.lane_evictions, scheduler.hotpath_routes, attn.bridge_fallbacks.
